How FuturesElite works

From your first challenge to live capital, step by step.

October 13, 2026

 

 

Every FuturesElite account follows the same path. You buy a challenge, pass one evaluation phase, verify your identity, trade a simulated funded account and request payouts. Consistent traders are invited to a live account with real capital.

The five stages

Buy a challenge. You can buy as many challenges as you like and there is no time limit to pass.

Pass the evaluation. One phase. Reach the profit target without hitting the loss limits, and meet your account's minimum days and consistency rule.

Verify and sign. Complete KYC with Veriff in your dashboard, then sign the funded trader contract.

Trade Sim Funded. Request payouts once your account's payout conditions are met.

Go live. The Risk Team invites traders to a live account. The usual path is your 4th consecutive payout.

 

 

Instant accounts skip the evaluation and start at the Sim Funded stage.

Good to know

Trading happens on simulated accounts until you go live.

Your dashboard shows the exact rules for each account you own: how much you can still lose, the daily loss limit, what is left to the target and your consistency share.

If something goes wrong technically during a challenge (an outage or a data feed problem), contact Support straight away.

Elite drawdown, daily loss limit and contracts

How the Max Loss Limit trails and locks, and how contract scaling works.

October 18, 2026

 

 

End of Day trailing drawdown

The Max Loss Limit is based on your closed balance at the end of each trading day.

A profitable day can move it up. A losing day leaves it where it is. Intraday swings and open profit never move it.

25K: once the account has made $1,000 of profit, the floor locks at $25,000 and stops trailing.

50K, 100K, 150K: the floor locks at $100 above the starting balance.

Close a day at or below the Max Loss Limit and the account is breached. A breach is final: reset the account or start a new challenge.

Daily loss limit

You choose at checkout, on every size: no daily loss limit (the default), or a soft-lock daily loss limit of $600 (25K), $1,200 (50K), $1,800 (100K) or $2,700 (150K). Choosing it lowers the price.

If you choose it, it applies in the evaluation and once funded. The level is measured from the higher of your balance and equity at the previous daily close.

A soft lock is not a breach. If your equity reaches it, trading is locked for 24 hours from that moment; the account stays open.

Daily loss limit: on Elite only if you chose it at checkout; always on for Prime, Ultra and Oracle; Nitro and Instant have none.

Contracts

In the evaluation you have the full allowance from day one: 2, 4, 8 or 12 contracts. Once funded, contracts scale with profit:

Elite checkout options

Choose your daily loss limit and consistency rule when you buy.

October 18, 2026

Every Elite size has two rules you configure at checkout. The price updates with your choices, and settings can't be changed after purchase. Your dashboard shows which settings each account uses.

Daily loss limit

None (default): the only loss rule is the Max Loss Limit.

Soft lock: $600 (25K), $1,200 (50K), $1,800 (100K) or $2,700 (150K), at a lower price. If your equity reaches it, trading is locked for 24 hours from that moment; the account stays open. The level is measured from the higher of your balance and equity at the previous daily close. It never counts as a breach, and it stops one bad session from ending the account. It applies in the evaluation and once funded.

Evaluation consistency

40% (default): no single day may be more than 40% of the profit used to pass. On a 25K ($1,250 target) your best day can be $500; on a 50K ($3,000 target), $1,200.

50%: more room and a minimum of 2 trading days, for a small extra fee. On a 25K your best day can be $625; on a 50K, $1,500.

Consistency in evaluation: your best single day may be at most 40% of your total profit (50% if you chose the 50% option at checkout). Exactly 40% (or 50%) passes. Elite evaluation needs at least 2 trading days; with the 40% rule you will in practice need at least 3 profitable days. Elite cannot be passed in one day. Elite funded accounts have no consistency rule.

Going over never fails the account: the target rises until your best day fits. Example at 40%: a $700 best day means you pass at $1,750 of profit.

How payouts are processed

From request to your bank or wallet.

Updated over a month ago

 

 

Request your payout from the dashboard once you qualify.

We review it. Payout requests are reviewed within 24–72 working hours (Monday–Friday). On average it takes about 24 hours to approve and 24 hours to process.

Approved payouts go to your Credits balance (Dashboard → Payouts).

Once approved, the payout is processed within 1–3 business days to Rise or crypto. Crypto payouts are limited to $500 per request; Rise has no limit. Or spend the credits on new challenges.

 

 

Rise

Create a free Rise account and complete a one-time KYC before your first payout.

Each cycle choose a local-currency bank transfer, stablecoins or crypto, or a split.

100+ crypto assets, 90+ currencies, 190+ countries.

Fees

Every payout has a 3% processing fee, whatever the route: Rise, crypto, or a refund to your original card or payment method. The fee is deducted from the amount sent.

Anti-money laundering

Trading hours and the 2% price-limit rule

When you can trade and when you must stop.

Updated over a week ago

 

 

Trading hours (Eastern Time)

A trading day runs from 6:00 PM to 4:55 PM the next day. A new day starts at 6:00 PM.

All positions must be closed by 4:55 PM ET every trading day; open positions are closed automatically at that time. The resulting profit or loss is yours.

Overnight holding is strictly prohibited. All positions must be closed before the daily market close. If a trader leaves a position open and the system fails to automatically close it, the trader remains fully responsible for any resulting profit or loss.

From 4:55 PM to 6:00 PM the market is on its daily break: no orders can be placed or changed.

The market is closed from Friday 4:55 PM to Sunday 6:00 PM. Holiday closures are announced in advance.

No positions may be held through the 4:55 PM close. Live accounts must be flat at least 15 minutes before the close.

 

 

The 2% price-limit rule

Stop trading a market once it has moved beyond its CME daily price limit minus 2 percentage points, in either direction.

Example: a 10,000 reference price with a 7% limit. Stop at 10,000 × (1 + 7% − 2%) = 10,500, or 10,000 × (1 − 7% + 2%) = 9,500. Breaking this rule can lead to restriction or termination.

Live accounts: loss floor, cushion and reserve

How a live account protects capital and pays you.

October 18, 2026

 

 

Loss floor

Every live account starts at $0 with a loss floor below it ($2,000 on a 50K).

The floor moves only at the daily close, to sit one floor-width below your best close. Intraday dips below it are safe if the day closes above.

Once it reaches $0 it stops there permanently.

If a trading day closes below the floor, the account is lost, including any cushion it holds. There is no daily loss limit.

Cushion

Half the starting floor ($1,000 on a 50K). Your first profits fill it.

Profit above the cushion is withdrawable from day one.

The cushion is released after 15 profitable days, not necessarily in a row. A day counts when realised profit reaches the daily minimum ($150 on a 50K).

Withdrawals never move the floor.

Reserve

Unlocks begin after 15 profitable live days and $5,000 of total live profit.

Then every extra $5,000 of profit unlocks $2,500.

Locked Reserve can't be withdrawn. Released Reserve can be withdrawn or used for margin.

Gambling, oversizing or reckless trading forfeits Reserve unlocks.

Getting paid

Payouts are daily with a $200 minimum: live profit above the cushion plus any released Reserve. The split is 90%.

Where Affiliates is in the menu and what each part of the page shows.

Updated over a month ago

 

Once your application is approved, we unlock the Affiliates page on your FuturesElite account. Until then, it doesn't appear in the menu.

How to open it

Sign in at app.futureselite.com.

Click your name in the top-right corner.

Choose Affiliates.

 

What's on the page

Copy affiliate link: your personal link. Traders who sign up through it become your affiliated users, and their purchases count toward your sales.

Totals: currently affiliated users, total sales and your total available payout.

Claim: request your available payout. Each request appears under Requests with its date, amount and status.

Monthly stats: new affiliated users, sales and number of orders for each month.

Advanced stats: charts grouped by day, week, month or all time. You can filter by sub-affiliate or pick a date range.

Orders, Accounts, Payouts and Commissions: the detail behind your numbers.

Don't see Affiliates in the menu? Your account hasn't been unlocked yet. It appears only after our team approves your application.

What you get as a partner, how to apply and what happens after you apply.

October 22, 2026

Our affiliate program is for creators and trading communities. Approved partners get their own community card on our Affiliates site, where communities are ranked by how much their traders have been paid.

What you get

Your own community profile: a shareable home for your community card, your traders' payouts and your social links.

Exclusive trader promos: give your audience a reason to use your code.

Commission on every sale made through your code.

Dedicated support: a contact to help you get started.

How to apply

Open our Affiliates site and click Get your community card.

Fill in the form: your full name, email address and community or brand name, at least one link where your community can be found, and a description of your community and how you'd work with FuturesElite (up to 1,000 characters). The size of your audience is optional.

Click Apply for your community card.

What happens next

Our team reviews your community and contacts you, using the details you gave us, to discuss the partnership.

If you're approved, we help you set up your profile and collect your logo and photo.

Your community card joins the lineup on our Affiliates site.

Applying doesn't create a card or confirm acceptance. We use the information you submit to review and respond to your application.

To see what a community card shows and how traders use your code, see Community cards and community codes.

How the community leaderboard and profiles work, and how traders use a community code.

October 22, 2026

Every approved partner gets a community card and a public profile on our Affiliates site.

The community leaderboard

Communities are ranked by the total paid out to the traders they referred.

View all communities lists every partner community, with search, sorting, a platform filter and a tab for new communities.

Community payout figures show what the traders referred by each community have been paid. They aren't the affiliate's commission or the affiliate's own trading results.

What a community profile shows

Community payouts: the total paid to traders referred by that community, all-time, in USD.

Traders paid, payout transactions and the largest trader payout.

About the community and links to its channels.

The community code, with a button to copy it.

Giveaways: rewards for traders who buy with the community's code, when the community has one running.

For traders: using a community code

Open the community's profile on our Affiliates site and copy its code.

Use the code when you buy your account.

Check the profile's Giveaways tab to see if there's a reward for buying with the code.

For affiliates: your card

After approval, we set up your profile with you and collect your logo and photo.

Use Share profile or Copy profile link to send your profile to your audience.

To apply, see Becoming a FuturesElite affiliate.
